scope: Exactly two fresh non-L14, US-primary scientific/big-physics candidates. No ledger, longlist, scorecard, selection, routing log, or state is modified.

binding_interpretation.G1: Two independent present-demand sources are required, including a primary buyer solicitation, buyer specification, funded program, or filing. A purchase order for the proposed startup feature is not required, but the purchased or funded category must be exact.
binding_interpretation.G7: The 2030 base case must remain open after known buyer design freezes and must cite two timing sources, including an official 2028-2035 trigger.
binding_interpretation.advance_rule: ADVANCE_TO_REDTEAM is used only when all seven literal hard gates pass on the evidence recorded here; an independent red team remains mandatory before final selection.

decision_summary.recommendation: Red-team rank 1 first. It has the strongest exact procurement evidence and an externally requested capability, but it is countable for 2030 only as an EIC Detector II/upgrade supplier, not as a late entrant to already-frozen base-ePIC photosensor procurement. Rank 2 is a credible independent backup in L16 if magnetic-background rejection survives the bounded experiment.

ranked_candidates.concept: Qualified diamond transmission-dynode membrane and integration cartridge for hybrid MCP-PMTs used in EIC-class photon detectors
named_buyer_examples: Brookhaven National Laboratory LDRD-26-055 hybrid MCP-PMT project
Brookhaven EIC Detector II instrumentation program if funded
US detector laboratories developing RICH, time-of-flight, and fast-photon systems
ranked_candidates.painful_job: Large-area MCP-PMTs lose photoelectrons at the first plate's non-pore area and must run high MCP gain to recover single photons, increasing accumulated charge and lifetime risk. Brookhaven's 2026 RFI is unusually exact: it asks outside organizations to supply and process thin diamond films, perform laser or RIE thickness reduction, create negative-electron-affinity surfaces, and measure secondary-electron yield for a hybrid MCP-PMT.
ranked_candidates.product: A reproducible, serialized transmission-dynode membrane package: thickness-controlled conductive CVD diamond, vacuum-stable negative-electron-affinity termination, guarded mount and electrode geometry, incoming electron-yield map, vacuum bake record, and a tube-integrator acceptance dossier. The startup supplies the difficult membrane/process interface and qualification data, not the MCP, photocathode, Timepix4 ASIC, or complete vacuum tube.
ranked_candidates.frontier_vision: Insert a thin, radiation-hard electron preamplifier ahead of any microchannel plate so detector builders can trade transmission gain for lower MCP voltage, longer life, and higher effective photon-detection efficiency across collider, neutron, medical, and ultrafast-imaging instruments.
ranked_candidates.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: reproduce published transmission-yield measurements on commercial CVD diamond coupons and negotiate test access with a US electron-source/vacuum lab. 2027: down-select thickness, doping, front electrode, and NEA treatment on at least 12 membranes. 2028: deliver four serialized dynode cartridges for independent SEY, vacuum-bake, and lifetime testing. 2029: require a paid BNL/US-lab qualification, funded Detector II work package, or signed tube-integrator design-in; a research collaboration without a purchasing path does not count.
ranked_candidates.launch_2030_timing_thesis: Base ePIC photosensor procurement is too early for a 2030 entrant and is explicitly excluded from the base case. The open socket is the separately named EIC Detector II hybrid-MCP-PMT program, post-installation upgrades, replacement lots, and other US fast-photon programs. BNL is doing enabling LDRD and outside-capability market research in 2026, while the EIC master schedule extends detector integration, installation, commissioning, and operations work through 2035. Four years is enough to qualify a supplied membrane/process module without attempting to design the complete detector tube.
ranked_candidates.demand_trigger_2030_2034: A funded EIC Detector II or ePIC upgrade/spares package that carries the hybrid MCP-PMT beyond LDRD, plus US detector programs purchasing radiation-tolerant, high-rate photon sensors during EIC commissioning and early operation. The trigger is valid only if at least one program funds external dynode hardware by end-2029.
ranked_candidates.competition_outlook_2030: Closest competitors are Incom's EIC HRPPD/LAPPD products, Exosens/Photonis Planacon and PhotonPix MCP-PMTs, Hamamatsu MCP-PMTs, and BNL's own tube architecture. Incom is already delivering EIC tiles and Exosens claims collection efficiency approaching 100 percent, so incumbent convergence is real. The non-cosmetic wedge is the qualified upstream diamond transmission-gain membrane/process cartridge, which can reduce the charge multiplication demanded from the MCP and is precisely the capability BNL is seeking externally; it is not a different package around an ordinary MCP.
ranked_candidates.timing_window_risk: EIC Detector II may never receive construction funding, Exosens or Incom may close the collection-efficiency gap without a dynode, or BNL may internalize the process after the LDRD. Do not count base-ePIC procurement. Kill the commercial thesis at end-2029 unless a US lab or tube maker pays for qualification or writes the cartridge into a funded post-freeze detector plan.
ranked_candidates.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034, with an earlier commercial kill at 2029-12-31 absent paid qualification or a funded design-in
ranked_candidates.extreme_edge: Target transmission secondary-electron gain of at least 8 at 1-3 keV while preserving timing and vacuum stability, allowing roughly an order-of-magnitude reduction in MCP charge gain for an equal downstream pulse in the validated operating point.
ranked_candidates.first_experiment: 2027-2028, nine months: procure at least 12 CVD diamond films spanning thickness and doping; laser/RIE thin them; apply two NEA treatments and two electrode schemes; map reflection and transmission electron yield in UHV before and after a 200 C bake and after an accumulated input charge test. Pass only if four membranes independently show transmission yield >=8 at <=3 keV, within-wafer yield coefficient of variation <=15%, dark current <=10 nA at the operating bias, <=10% yield loss after bake, and <=20% loss after the accelerated charge dose. Kill on surface instability in air transfer, destructive charging, timing spread >50 ps attributable to the dynode in a pulsed-electron test, or if two tube integrators say the mount cannot be sealed.
ranked_candidates.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: Respond to a follow-on BNL procurement or partner with a US MCP-PMT integrator in 2028; by 2029 require a paid qualification lot, funded EIC Detector II work package, or signed integration specification.
ranked_candidates.safety_regulatory_export_path: The product is a passive vacuum component, but operation uses kilovolt bias and UHV processing; use interlocked electron-gun/HV stations, vacuum-material traceability, contamination controls, and buyer radiation-qualification procedures. US civilian DOE science is the base case. Classify the detector component and screen end use before any export; no cross-border route is required.
ranked_candidates.founder_fit_note: Thin-film process control, electronics test, high-voltage measurement, statistical qualification, and supplier automation use generic EE/CE skills; NEA surface chemistry and vacuum-tube sealing require specialist partners.

G1.rationale: BNL RFI 479547 is an exact external-capability request; separate BNL LDRD and EIC records name the Detector II project and current HRPPD orders.

G2.rationale: Six technical journal works have final publisher/DOI evidence; no preprint carries a load-bearing physics claim.

G3.rationale: The nine-month $94k membrane matrix has numerical yield, uniformity, leakage, bake, dose, timing, and integrator-interface kills.

G4.rationale: Incom, Exosens/Photonis, Hamamatsu, and BNL in-house architecture are named. The upstream transmission-gain membrane is a functional multiplication stage that BNL is explicitly sourcing externally.

G5.rationale: Peer-reviewed diamond transmission and NEA emission measurements establish the mechanism; the experiment tests the unproven repeatability and lifetime.

G6.rationale: HV/UHV safety, materials traceability, radiation qualification, US-only base case, and export/end-use screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: The plan excludes frozen base-ePIC procurement, uses a 2026 external RFI plus FY27 Detector II work, cites the official EIC schedule through 2035, and has a hard end-2029 commercial kill.

ranked_candidates.distinctness_check: Fresh L13 detector-material subsystem; not detector timing, SRF LLRF/piezo, D-16 Brayton, A-05 NEG coating, D-19, A-02, A-21, or A-22.

ranked_candidates.concept: Self-referenced clamp-on Lorentz-force flowmeter for opaque liquid-metal fusion loops
named_buyer_examples: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory LEAP and LMX-U liquid-metal program
DOE FIRE Collaborative liquid-metal test facilities
US fusion blanket and plasma-facing-component test loops
ranked_candidates.painful_job: Opaque, reactive liquid lithium and blanket metals cannot be inspected optically, while wetted electrodes, acoustic couplants, and penetrations complicate high-temperature, high-field loops. PPPL started a dedicated liquid-metal ultrasonic diagnostic project in 2026 and DOE's June 2026 roadmap requires high-field MHD loops, minimum flow-sensing architecture, and loop-scale monitoring, demonstrating present instrument demand rather than generic fusion enthusiasm.
ranked_candidates.product: A removable two-head Lorentz-force flowmeter that clamps outside a nonmagnetic flow channel. Matched magnet/force-sensor heads, synchronous modulation, a background reference, temperature/conductivity estimation, and dry-calibration artifacts estimate bulk flow without a wetted transducer. The safety controller remains independent; the instrument is a metrology channel, not a flow actuator.
ranked_candidates.frontier_vision: Give every opaque liquid-metal test loop a traceable, zero-penetration flow channel that survives chemistry changes and becomes the validation layer for fusion blanket digital twins.
ranked_candidates.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: reproduce published Lorentz-force flow measurements in a bench GaInSn channel. 2027: build paired gradiometric heads and dry-calibration fixtures. 2028: compare against gravimetric and ultrasonic references in a Galinstan loop under controlled transverse background fields. 2029: require a paid PPPL/US-lab lithium-loop qualification or a written FIRE-facility procurement path.
ranked_candidates.launch_2030_timing_thesis: PPPL launched the national liquid-metal research program and a dedicated flow diagnostic in 2026. DOE's official roadmap calls for expanded D/H loops and diagnostic architecture in two to three years, high-field MHD and blanket test facilities in three to five years, and integrated sensing in five to ten years. A 2030 product therefore enters during facility buildout and lithium qualification, after proving itself in surrogate metal, without displacing a frozen machine design.
ranked_candidates.demand_trigger_2030_2034: Commissioning and operation of PPPL LEAP/national FIRE liquid-metal platforms and DOE roadmap mid-term high-field MHD/blanket facilities in 2029-2031, followed by real-time embedded diagnostic qualification through 2034.
ranked_candidates.competition_outlook_2030: Closest alternatives are PPPL's in-house liquid-metal ultrasonic diagnostic, Met-Flow/Dantec ultrasonic velocity profilers, Siemens SITRANS electromagnetic flowmeters, and gravimetric or electrode probes. The non-cosmetic wedge is paired force measurement through the pipe wall with no wetted electrodes or acoustic path plus synchronous background-field rejection and transferable dry calibration; PPPL's disclosed project uses ultrasound, not this architecture.
ranked_candidates.timing_window_risk: The external tokamak or loop magnet can swamp micro-newton force signals, conductive structures can distort calibration, and PPPL's ultrasonic approach may prove adequate. Kill if paired heads cannot reject background-field and vibration error below the flow signal or if users will not allocate straight-pipe length for the clamp.
ranked_candidates.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034, with an earlier commercial kill at 2029-12-31 absent paid lithium-loop qualification or written facility procurement path
ranked_candidates.extreme_edge: Eliminate all wetted flow-sensor parts and target 40 dB common-mode rejection of field/vibration background while holding bulk-flow error to <=5 percent, aiming for at least a tenfold reduction in sensor-service interventions versus probes inside a reactive-metal boundary.
ranked_candidates.first_experiment: 2027-2028, 12 months: build two paired Lorentz-force heads around a nonmagnetic Galinstan channel; sweep 0.05-1.0 m/s, temperature, conductivity, vibration, pipe-wall thickness, and a 0-0.5 T transverse background; compare with timed mass transfer and an ultrasonic profiler for 100 hours. Pass only if RMS bulk-flow error <=5%, zero drift <=2% full scale over 24 hours, background rejection >=40 dB, calibration transfer between heads <=3%, and inferred Lorentz braking adds <1% pressure loss. Kill if background-field error exceeds 5%, thermal drift is not correctable with one measured temperature, or dry calibration fails after re-clamping.
ranked_candidates.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: 2028 joint comparison on PPPL-like Galinstan hardware; 2029 paid lithium-loop qualification, FIRE work package, or written approved-instrument interface. An academic paper alone does not count.
ranked_candidates.safety_regulatory_export_path: Precompany work uses nonradioactive Galinstan. Lithium testing occurs only in a buyer-operated inert-atmosphere facility with fire, spill, pressure-boundary, lockout, and hazardous-material procedures. The meter stays outside the primary boundary and is not credited as a safety interlock. US civilian facilities are the base case; later foreign sales require export/end-use screening.
ranked_candidates.founder_fit_note: Low-noise sensing, synchronous demodulation, embedded control, inverse calibration, and automated test fit generic EE/CE skills; liquid-lithium operations and fusion safety require lab partners.

G1.rationale: PPPL names an active liquid-metal ultrasonic diagnostic and operating facilities; the independent DOE roadmap mandates flow diagnostics and high-field MHD/blanket test infrastructure.

G2.rationale: Seven technical works have final journal/DOI evidence; preprints are not used for load-bearing claims.

G3.rationale: The 12-month $89k test has numerical flow error, drift, rejection, calibration-transfer, and backreaction kills.

G4.rationale: PPPL ultrasound, Met-Flow/Dantec UVP, Siemens electromagnetic meters, and gravimetric/electrode probes are named; the paired external force architecture is functionally distinct and not PPPL's disclosed build.

G5.rationale: Lorentz-force velocimetry has peer-reviewed laboratory and plant validation; the experiment directly tests the fusion-specific background problem.

G6.rationale: Galinstan-first testing, buyer-facility lithium safety, no safety-interlock credit, US base case, and export screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: PPPL's 2026 program, DOE's official 2-3, 3-5, and 5-10 year milestones, bounded precompany work, TRL 7 target, and end-2029 engagement kill establish a post-freeze 2030 socket.

ranked_candidates.distinctness_check: Fresh L16 electromagnetic process instrument; not detector timing, SRF LLRF/piezo, D-16 Brayton, A-05 NEG coating, D-19, A-02, A-21, or A-22, and it does not consume a capped L03/L04/L06/L14 slot.
